events.text: Thomas Edison announces the phonograph, a machine that can record and replay sound.
Emile Berliner patents the gramophone and its flat-disc record system.
Irving Berlin publishes “Alexander’s Ragtime Band,” a Tin Pan Alley sensation.
“Livery Stable Blues,” widely cited as the first jazz record, is released.
Mamie Smith records “Crazy Blues,” opening a major market for blues records.
Louis Armstrong makes his first recordings as a member of King Oliver’s Creole Jazz Band.
Electrical recording replaces acoustic horns and changes how records can sound.
Nashville’s WSM begins the barn-dance broadcast that becomes the Grand Ole Opry.
Show Boat opens on Broadway, reshaping the American musical with integrated storytelling.
The Bristol sessions capture the Carter Family and Jimmie Rodgers, country music’s “big bang.”
Benny Goodman’s Palomar Ballroom engagement ignites the swing era.
Robert Johnson makes his first recordings in San Antonio, Texas.
Benny Goodman brings jazz to Carnegie Hall in a landmark concert.
Billie Holiday records “Strange Fruit,” turning a protest song into an American standard.
Billboard publishes its first “Best Selling Retail Records” chart.
A recording ban begins as musicians seek royalties from record companies.
Oklahoma! opens on Broadway, the first Rodgers and Hammerstein musical.
Charlie Parker records “Ko-Ko” with Dizzy Gillespie, a bebop landmark.
Atlantic Records is founded in New York City.
Columbia introduces the 33⅓ rpm long-playing record.
RCA Victor introduces the 45 rpm single format.
Fender introduces the solid-body electric guitar soon renamed the Telecaster.

events.artist: Jackie Brenston and His Delta Cats
events.text: “Rocket 88” is released, often called one of rock ’n’ roll’s first records.
Sam Phillips founds Sun Records in Memphis.
Gibson introduces the Les Paul solid-body electric guitar.
Hank Williams dies in the back seat of a Cadillac on the way to a New Year’s Day show.
Bill Haley & His Comets record “Rock Around the Clock.”
Fender introduces the Stratocaster.
Chuck Berry releases “Maybellene,” a defining early rock ’n’ roll single.
Little Richard’s “Tutti Frutti” arrives with its electrifying opening cry.
Fats Domino takes “Blueberry Hill” to a huge pop audience.
“That’ll Be the Day” becomes Buddy Holly and the Crickets’ breakthrough hit.
West Side Story opens on Broadway.
Commercial stereo LPs begin to reach listeners.
Billboard launches the Hot 100 singles chart.
Miles Davis releases Kind of Blue, one of jazz’s landmark albums.

events.artist: Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens & the Big Bopper
events.text: A plane crash in Iowa kills Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens and the Big Bopper.
The first Grammy Awards are presented.
Berry Gordy incorporates Motown Record Corporation in Detroit.
Patsy Cline records Willie Nelson’s “Crazy.”
Ray Charles releases Modern Sounds in Country and Western Music.
The Rolling Stones play their first gig at London’s Marquee Club.
Bob Dylan releases The Freewheelin’ Bob Dylan, including “Blowin’ in the Wind.”
Philips introduces the compact cassette.
Sam Cooke records “A Change Is Gonna Come.”
Robert Moog unveils his modular synthesizer.
“Where Did Our Love Go” gives the Supremes their first No. 1 hit.
John Coltrane records A Love Supreme in a single session.
Bob Dylan plugs in at the Newport Folk Festival.
James Brown’s “Papa’s Got a Brand New Bag” points the way to funk.
The Rolling Stones release “(I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction.”
The Beach Boys release Pet Sounds.
The Monterey International Pop Festival brings rock’s counterculture to a vast audience.
Aretha Franklin’s “Respect” makes a definitive claim for freedom and dignity.
The Velvet Underground & Nico arrives with its Andy Warhol banana cover.
The Jimi Hendrix Experience release Are You Experienced.
The first issue of Rolling Stone magazine is published in San Francisco.
Johnny Cash records At Folsom Prison before an audience of inmates.
Wendy Carlos’s Switched-On Bach makes the Moog synthesizer a best-seller.
The Woodstock Music and Art Fair becomes a defining counterculture gathering.
Violence at Altamont darkens the 1960s festival ideal.
Led Zeppelin release their self-titled debut album.
Black Sabbath release their self-titled debut, a foundational heavy-metal record.
Miles Davis releases Bitches Brew, a jazz-fusion watershed.
The first festival is held at Worthy Farm, the start of Glastonbury.
Marvin Gaye releases What’s Going On.
Carole King releases Tapestry.
Joni Mitchell releases Blue.
The Rolling Stones release Exile on Main St.
Stevie Wonder releases Talking Book, featuring “Superstition.”
The film The Harder They Come and its soundtrack carry reggae abroad.
DJ Kool Herc’s Bronx party is widely remembered as a birth moment for hip-hop.
Pink Floyd release The Dark Side of the Moon.
The Wailers release Catch a Fire, their Island Records debut.
Kraftwerk release Autobahn and take electronic music toward the pop mainstream.
ABBA win the Eurovision Song Contest with “Waterloo.”
Bruce Springsteen releases Born to Run.
Queen release “Bohemian Rhapsody.”
Patti Smith releases Horses.
Ramones release their fast, stripped-down self-titled debut.
The Sex Pistols release “Anarchy in the U.K.”
Stevie Wonder releases the double album Songs in the Key of Life.
The Saturday Night Fever soundtrack turns disco into a global commercial force.
Fleetwood Mac release Rumours.
Donna Summer and Giorgio Moroder’s “I Feel Love” previews the electronic future of dance music.
Studio 54 opens in Manhattan.
Martin Scorsese’s concert film The Last Waltz brings The Band’s farewell to cinemas.
“Rapper’s Delight” takes hip-hop onto the pop charts.
Sony launches the Walkman, making private portable listening ubiquitous.
The Clash release London Calling in the U.K.
A crate of disco records is blown up at Chicago’s Comiskey Park.
AC/DC release Back in Black, their first album with Brian Johnson.
Roland introduces the TR-808 drum machine.
MTV goes on the air with “Video Killed the Radio Star.”

events.artist: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five
events.text: “The Message” expands hip-hop’s social and storytelling ambitions.
The first compact discs and CD players go on sale.
Madonna releases her self-titled debut album.
The MIDI standard lets synthesizers from different makers talk to each other.
Metallica release their debut, Kill ’Em All.
Run-D.M.C. release their hard-hitting self-titled debut.
Madonna performs “Like a Virgin” at the first MTV Video Music Awards.
Bruce Springsteen releases Born in the U.S.A.
The global Live Aid concerts raise funds for famine relief in Ethiopia.
An all-star chorus records “We Are the World.”
Whitney Houston releases her self-titled debut album.
Beastie Boys release Licensed to Ill, the first rap LP to top the Billboard 200.
Run-D.M.C. and Aerosmith’s “Walk This Way” knocks down the wall between rap and rock.
Paul Simon releases Graceland, recorded with South African musicians.

events.artist: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
events.text: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inducts its first class.
“Jack Your Body” makes Chicago house a U.K. No. 1 single.
U2 release The Joshua Tree.
Guns N’ Roses release Appetite for Destruction.
N.W.A release Straight Outta Compton.
Public Enemy release It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back.
De La Soul release 3 Feet High and Rising, a playful sample-rich rap landmark.
The Stone Roses release their self-titled debut.
Janet Jackson releases Rhythm Nation 1814.
Public Enemy release Fear of a Black Planet.
Sinéad O’Connor’s “Nothing Compares 2 U” tops charts around the world.
Nirvana release Nevermind, bringing grunge into the global mainstream.
The first Lollapalooza tour takes alternative rock on the road.
A Tribe Called Quest release The Low End Theory.
Billboard charts switch to SoundScan’s point-of-sale data, reshaping the rankings overnight.
Dr. Dre releases The Chronic, a defining G-funk record.
Whitney Houston’s “I Will Always Love You” begins a record-setting run at No. 1.
Wu-Tang Clan release Enter the Wu-Tang (36 Chambers).
Björk releases Debut.
Nas releases Illmatic, an East Coast rap classic.
Kurt Cobain is found dead at his Seattle home.
Green Day release Dookie, taking pop-punk to the mainstream.
The Notorious B.I.G. releases Ready to Die.
Alanis Morissette releases Jagged Little Pill.
Tejano star Selena is shot and killed at age 23.
D’Angelo releases Brown Sugar, a neo-soul cornerstone.
Fugees release The Score, a crossover rap and R&B success.
Spice Girls release their debut single, “Wannabe.”
Tupac Shakur dies after a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas.
Daft Punk release Homework, a dance-music touchstone.
The Buena Vista Social Club album brings veteran Cuban musicians to a world audience.
Erykah Badu releases Baduizm.
Lauryn Hill releases The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill.
Cher’s “Believe” turns Auto-Tune into a pop effect.
Britney Spears releases her debut single, “...Baby One More Time.”
Napster launches, making peer-to-peer music sharing a defining industry disruption.
The first Coachella festival is held in the California desert.
OutKast release Stankonia.
Eminem releases The Marshall Mathers LP.
Apple introduces the first iPod.
The Strokes release Is This It, sparking a garage-rock revival.
Jay-Z releases The Blueprint.
Missy Elliott releases Under Construction.
American Idol premieres on U.S. television.
Norah Jones releases Come Away with Me.
Apple opens the iTunes Music Store.
50 Cent releases Get Rich or Die Tryin’.
The White Stripes release “Seven Nation Army,” a future stadium chant.
Kanye West releases The College Dropout.
Arcade Fire release their debut album, Funeral.
Green Day release the rock opera American Idiot.
YouTube launches, soon becoming a major place for music discovery and video.
Arctic Monkeys’ debut single “I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor” enters the U.K. chart at No. 1.
Justin Timberlake releases FutureSex/LoveSounds.
Daft Punk unveil their pyramid stage show at Coachella.
Taylor Swift releases her self-titled debut album.
Spotify is founded in Stockholm.
Rihanna releases “Umbrella.”
Beyoncé releases “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It).”
Lil Wayne releases Tha Carter III.
Kanye West releases the Auto-Tune-soaked 808s & Heartbreak.
Lady Gaga’s The Fame turns her into a pop phenomenon.
Kanye West interrupts Taylor Swift’s acceptance speech at the MTV Video Music Awards.
Kanye West releases My Beautiful Dark Twisted Fantasy.
Drake releases his debut studio album, Thank Me Later.
Adele releases 21, the album that becomes a worldwide juggernaut.
Spotify launches in the United States.
Kendrick Lamar releases good kid, m.A.A.d city.
“Gangnam Style” becomes the first YouTube video to reach a billion views.
Frank Ocean releases Channel Orange.
Beyoncé unexpectedly releases her self-titled visual album.
Daft Punk release Random Access Memories, led by “Get Lucky.”
Lorde’s “Royals” makes a New Zealand teenager a global star.
U2’s Songs of Innocence is pushed free to half a billion iTunes customers.
D’Angelo ends a long silence with the surprise release of Black Messiah.
Kendrick Lamar releases To Pimp a Butterfly.
Hamilton opens on Broadway.
Apple launches its Apple Music streaming service.
Beyoncé releases Lemonade with a film-length visual companion.
Frank Ocean releases Blonde.
Bob Dylan is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
“Despacito” becomes a global streaming-era crossover phenomenon.
Kendrick Lamar releases DAMN.
Cardi B releases Invasion of Privacy.
Kendrick Lamar becomes the first rapper to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music.
Beyoncé headlines Coachella with a marching-band homage to Black college culture.
BTS become the first K-pop act to top the Billboard 200.
“Old Town Road” breaks the record for the longest Billboard Hot 100 run at No. 1.
Billie Eilish releases When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?
Taylor Swift surprise-releases folklore during the pandemic.
BTS score their first Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 with “Dynamite.”
Olivia Rodrigo releases SOUR, a huge Gen Z pop debut.
Taylor Swift releases Fearless (Taylor’s Version), the first of her re-recorded albums.
Beyoncé releases RENAISSANCE, celebrating Black dance-music lineages.
Bad Bunny releases Un Verano Sin Ti.
A Stranger Things placement sends Kate Bush’s “Running Up That Hill” back up the charts.
boygenius release the record.
Taylor Swift opens the Eras Tour in Glendale, Arizona.
Charli xcx releases BRAT and sparks a neon-green pop-cultural moment.
Beyoncé releases Cowboy Carter.
Kendrick Lamar releases “Not Like Us.”
Kendrick Lamar headlines the Super Bowl halftime show in New Orleans.
Black Sabbath’s original lineup plays a farewell concert in Birmingham.
John Lennon’s Quarry Men meet Paul McCartney at a Liverpool church fête.
The Beatles begin their formative residencies in Hamburg clubs.
The Beatles make their first appearance at Liverpool’s Cavern Club.
The Beatles release their first single, “Love Me Do.”
Ringo Starr replaces Pete Best as the Beatles’ drummer.
The Beatles record most of Please Please Me in one long Abbey Road session.
The Beatles make their first appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show.
“I Want to Hold Your Hand” reaches No. 1 in the U.S., setting off Beatlemania there.
The Beatles star in their first feature film, A Hard Day’s Night.
The Beatles play Shea Stadium, setting a new scale for rock concerts.
The Beatles release Rubber Soul.
The Beatles release Revolver.
The Beatles play their last ticketed concert at San Francisco’s Candlestick Park.
“Strawberry Fields Forever” pushes studio pop into kaleidoscopic territory.
The Beatles release Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band.
The Beatles perform “All You Need Is Love” on the global satellite broadcast Our World.
The Beatles release their sprawling self-titled double album, the White Album.
“Hey Jude” is released as the first Beatles single on Apple Records.
The Beatles give their final public performance on the Apple Corps rooftop.
The Beatles release Abbey Road.
Paul McCartney announces he is no longer working with the Beatles.
The Beatles’ final album release, Let It Be, arrives.
John Lennon is shot and killed outside the Dakota in New York.
The Beatles are inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
The Beatles Anthology television series and “Free as a Bird” revive the group’s story.
The chart-topper compilation 1 sells millions to a new generation.
George Harrison dies in Los Angeles.
Peter Jackson’s documentary series The Beatles: Get Back premieres.
The Beatles release “Now and Then,” completed from a John Lennon demo with new audio technology.
David Bowie releases his self-titled debut album.
David Bowie releases “Space Oddity,” introducing Major Tom.
David Bowie releases Hunky Dory.
David Bowie releases The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust and the Spiders from Mars.
David Bowie releases Aladdin Sane.
David Bowie retires Ziggy Stardust onstage at the Hammersmith Odeon.
David Bowie releases Diamond Dogs.
David Bowie releases Young Americans and reaches No. 1 in the U.S. with “Fame.”
David Bowie releases Station to Station.
David Bowie stars in Nicolas Roeg’s film The Man Who Fell to Earth.
David Bowie releases Low, the first piece of his Berlin trilogy.
David Bowie releases “Heroes.”
David Bowie releases Lodger.
David Bowie releases Scary Monsters (and Super Creeps).
David Bowie and Queen release “Under Pressure.”
David Bowie releases Let’s Dance.
David Bowie releases Tonight.
David Bowie and Mick Jagger release “Dancing in the Street” for Live Aid.
David Bowie plays Jareth the Goblin King in Labyrinth.
David Bowie’s band Tin Machine release their debut album.
David Bowie releases Black Tie White Noise.
David Bowie releases the dystopian, Brian Eno-assisted 1. Outside.
David Bowie is inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
David Bowie releases the drum-and-bass-inflected Earthling.
David Bowie reunites with producer Tony Visconti for Heathen.
David Bowie releases Reality and begins his final world tour.
An emergency heart procedure cuts short David Bowie’s final tour.
David Bowie unexpectedly returns with The Next Day.
David Bowie releases Blackstar two days before his death.
Prince releases his debut album, For You, credited as its sole producer and performer.
Prince releases his self-titled sophomore album.
Prince releases Dirty Mind.
Prince releases Controversy.
Prince releases 1999.
“Little Red Corvette” gives Prince his first U.S. top-ten single.
Prince releases Purple Rain, with its hit film arriving weeks later.
Prince releases Around the World in a Day.
Prince releases Parade, the soundtrack to Under the Cherry Moon.
Prince releases Sign o’ the Times.
Prince opens his Paisley Park studio complex in Chanhassen, Minnesota.
Prince releases Lovesexy.
Prince releases Batman, his soundtrack for Tim Burton’s film.
Prince releases the film and album Graffiti Bridge.

events.artist: Prince and the New Power Generation
events.text: Prince releases Diamonds and Pearls.
Prince releases the unpronounceable Love Symbol Album.
Prince changes his name to an unpronounceable symbol.
Prince releases Come while fighting Warner Bros. over artistic control.
“The Most Beautiful Girl in the World” becomes an independent hit for Prince.
Prince releases The Gold Experience.
Prince releases the three-disc Emancipation after regaining freedom from Warner Bros.
Prince releases Rave Un2 the Joy Fantastic.
Prince reclaims his name as his publishing contract expires.
Prince returns to the mainstream with Musicology.
Prince releases 3121, his first album to debut at No. 1 in the U.S.
Prince performs a rain-soaked “Purple Rain” during the Super Bowl halftime show.
Prince returns to Warner Bros. and releases Art Official Age.
Prince dies at Paisley Park, prompting a worldwide outpouring of tribute.
The shelved Prince album Welcome 2 America is released posthumously.
Nick Rhodes and John Taylor form the early version of Duran Duran in Birmingham.
Duran Duran become resident band at Birmingham’s Rum Runner nightclub.
Duran Duran release their self-titled debut album.
Duran Duran release Rio, making them central to the New Romantic explosion.
The Sri Lanka-shot video for “Hungry Like the Wolf” helps launch the band in America.
Duran Duran release Seven and the Ragged Tiger.
“Is There Something I Should Know?” enters the U.K. chart at No. 1.
Duran Duran join Band Aid’s “Do They Know It’s Christmas?” session.
“The Reflex” tops the charts on both sides of the Atlantic.
Duran Duran release “A View to a Kill,” the only Bond theme to top the U.S. chart.
Duran Duran’s members release albums as the side projects the Power Station and Arcadia.
Duran Duran return as a trio with Notorious.
Duran Duran release Big Thing and explore house-influenced pop.
Duran Duran release Liberty.
Duran Duran’s “Wedding Album” brings “Ordinary World” and “Come Undone.”
Duran Duran release the covers album Thank You.
Duran Duran release Medazzaland as John Taylor departs.
Duran Duran release Pop Trash.
The original five members reunite for Astronaut.
Duran Duran release Red Carpet Massacre, made with Timbaland and Justin Timberlake.
Duran Duran headline the Hyde Park concert marking the London Olympics opening ceremony.
Duran Duran release Paper Gods.
Duran Duran release Future Past, produced with Erol Alkan and Mark Ronson.
Duran Duran are inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Duran Duran release Danse Macabre, a Halloween-themed set of new songs and covers.
The Jackson brothers form a group in Gary, Indiana.
The Jackson 5 sign with Motown and release “I Want You Back.”
The Jackson 5 reach No. 1 with “ABC.”
“I’ll Be There” becomes the Jackson 5’s fourth consecutive No. 1 single.
Michael Jackson launches his solo career with “Got to Be There.”
Michael Jackson’s “Ben” becomes his first solo No. 1 single.
The Jackson 5 leave Motown for Epic and rename themselves the Jacksons.
The Jacksons release Destiny, including “Shake Your Body (Down to the Ground).”
Michael Jackson plays the Scarecrow in the film The Wiz.
Michael Jackson releases Off the Wall, produced by Quincy Jones.
The Jacksons release Triumph.
Michael Jackson releases Thriller.
Michael Jackson premieres the moonwalk during Motown 25.
The 14-minute “Thriller” video premieres.
The Victory Tour brings the Jackson brothers to stadiums across North America.
Michael Jackson wins a record eight Grammy Awards in one night.
Michael Jackson buys ATV Music and its catalog of Beatles songs.
Michael Jackson’s 3D film Captain EO opens at Disney theme parks.
Michael Jackson releases Bad.
Michael Jackson releases Dangerous.
Michael Jackson turns the Super Bowl halftime show into a global pop spectacle.
Michael Jackson marries Lisa Marie Presley.
Michael Jackson releases HIStory: Past, Present and Future, Book I.
The Jackson 5 are inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Michael Jackson releases Invincible.
A California jury acquits Michael Jackson on all counts.
The death of Michael Jackson halts the planned This Is It London residency.
Four of the Jackson brothers reunite for the Unity Tour.
MJ the Musical opens on Broadway.
New Edition form in Boston’s Orchard Park projects.
New Edition release their debut album, Candy Girl.
New Edition score a crossover hit with “Cool It Now.”
New Edition release All for Love.
New Edition release the doo-wop covers album Under the Blue Moon.
New Edition release Heart Break with Johnny Gill in the group.
New Edition offshoot Bell Biv DeVoe release Poison.
New Edition reunite their classic lineup for Home Again.
New Edition release One Love on Bad Boy Records.
New Edition receive BET’s Lifetime Achievement Award.
The BET miniseries The New Edition Story brings the group’s history to television.
New Edition headline the Culture Tour with Charlie Wilson and Jodeci.
New Edition begin a Las Vegas residency.
Elvis Presley records “That’s All Right” at Sun Studio.
RCA Victor buys Elvis Presley’s contract from Sun Records.
Elvis Presley’s “Heartbreak Hotel” becomes his first No. 1 hit.
Elvis Presley makes the first of three appearances on The Ed Sullivan Show.
Elvis Presley buys Graceland.
Elvis Presley stars in Jailhouse Rock.
Elvis Presley enters the U.S. Army.
Elvis Presley returns from the Army and releases G.I. Blues.
Elvis Presley stars in Blue Hawaii, whose soundtrack includes “Can’t Help Falling in Love.”
Elvis Presley stars opposite Ann-Margret in Viva Las Vegas.
Elvis Presley marries Priscilla Beaulieu in Las Vegas.
Elvis Presley’s black-leather comeback special reconnects him with live rock ’n’ roll.
Elvis Presley begins his landmark Las Vegas residency at the International Hotel.
“Suspicious Minds” becomes Elvis Presley’s final U.S. No. 1 single.
Elvis Presley meets President Richard Nixon at the White House.
Elvis Presley sells out four shows at Madison Square Garden.
Elvis Presley’s Aloha from Hawaii is broadcast live via satellite.
Elvis Presley dies at Graceland.
Graceland opens to the public.
A JXL remix of “A Little Less Conversation” puts Elvis Presley back at No. 1 in the U.K.
Baz Luhrmann’s biopic Elvis, starring Austin Butler, reaches cinemas.
Nina Simone releases her debut, Little Girl Blue, including “I Loves You, Porgy.”
Nina Simone records Nina Simone at Town Hall in New York.
Nina Simone records Nina Simone at Carnegie Hall.
Nina Simone writes and performs “Mississippi Goddam” as a civil-rights protest.
Nina Simone releases I Put a Spell on You.
Nina Simone releases Pastel Blues, closing with a ten-minute “Sinnerman.”
Nina Simone releases Wild Is the Wind.
Nina Simone releases Silk & Soul.
Nina Simone releases ’Nuff Said!, recorded days after Martin Luther King Jr.’s assassination.
Nina Simone’s “Ain’t Got No, I Got Life” becomes a British hit.
Nina Simone records “To Be Young, Gifted and Black” in concert.
Nina Simone releases Black Gold.
Nina Simone leaves the United States for Barbados.
Nina Simone gives a celebrated, confrontational performance at the Montreux Jazz Festival.
A perfume commercial turns Nina Simone’s “My Baby Just Cares for Me” into a U.K. hit.
Nina Simone releases her final studio album, A Single Woman.
Nina Simone dies at her home in southern France.
The documentary What Happened, Miss Simone? premieres.
Nina Simone is inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Amy Winehouse releases her debut album, Frank.
Amy Winehouse wins an Ivor Novello Award for “Stronger Than Me.”
Amy Winehouse releases Back to Black.
Amy Winehouse wins the Brit Award for Best British Female Solo Artist.
Amy Winehouse sings “Valerie” on Mark Ronson’s album Version.
Amy Winehouse wins five Grammy Awards, including Record of the Year.
Amy Winehouse dies in London at age 27.
The posthumous collection Lioness: Hidden Treasures is released.
A bronze statue of Amy Winehouse is unveiled in Camden.
Asif Kapadia’s documentary Amy is released.
The biographical film Back to Black brings Amy Winehouse’s story to cinemas.
Kevin Parker begins releasing early Tame Impala recordings.
Tame Impala release their self-titled debut EP on Modular.
Tame Impala release their debut album, Innerspeaker.
Tame Impala release Lonerism.
Tame Impala release the album Live Versions.
Tame Impala release Currents, led by “Let It Happen.”
Rihanna covers Tame Impala’s “New Person, Same Old Mistakes” on Anti.
Tame Impala headline Coachella.
Tame Impala release The Slow Rush.
Tame Impala continue their worldwide touring as Kevin Parker’s project enters a new era.
Tame Impala release Deadbeat.
The schoolfriends who will become Radiohead form On a Friday in Abingdon.
On a Friday sign to EMI, soon renaming themselves Radiohead.
Radiohead release “Creep.”
Radiohead release their debut album, Pablo Honey.
Radiohead release the My Iron Lung EP.
Radiohead release The Bends.
Radiohead release OK Computer.
The tour documentary Meeting People Is Easy is released.
Radiohead release Kid A, pivoting into electronic textures and abstraction.
Radiohead release Amnesiac.
Radiohead release Hail to the Thief.
Thom Yorke releases his first solo album, The Eraser.
Radiohead release In Rainbows with a pay-what-you-want download.
Radiohead release The King of Limbs.
Radiohead release A Moon Shaped Pool.
Radiohead reissue OK Computer as OKNOTOK with unreleased songs.
Radiohead are inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Thom Yorke and Jonny Greenwood debut their project the Smile at Glastonbury’s livestream event.
Radiohead play their first concerts in seven years.
Blur release their debut album, Leisure.
Blur release Modern Life Is Rubbish, a key early Britpop statement.
Blur release Parklife.
Blur sweep the Brit Awards after the success of Parklife.
Blur release The Great Escape.
Blur release “Song 2,” their noisy international hit.
Blur release 13, a raw and experimental breakup album.
Blur release The Magic Whip, their first album in twelve years.
Blur release The Ballad of Darren.
Blur release Think Tank, made largely without Graham Coxon.
Blur’s reunited original lineup plays London’s Hyde Park.
Damon Albarn’s cartoon band Gorillaz release their self-titled debut.
Blur’s “Country House” beats Oasis’s “Roll With It” to No. 1 in the Battle of Britpop.
Oasis release Definitely Maybe, then the fastest-selling debut in British history.
Oasis release (What’s the Story) Morning Glory?
Oasis play two nights at Knebworth Park for a quarter-million people.
Oasis release Be Here Now amid immense anticipation.
Noel Gallagher announces he has left Oasis, ending the band’s original run.
Oasis announce a reunion tour, rekindling Britpop-era fever.
Alan McGee signs Oasis to Creation Records after seeing them in Glasgow.
Noel Gallagher attends Tony Blair’s Downing Street reception.
Oasis release Standing on the Shoulder of Giants.
Oasis release Don’t Believe the Truth.
Oasis open their reunion tour in Cardiff.
Suede release their Mercury Prize-winning self-titled debut.
Suede release Dog Man Star.
Suede release Coming Up, a glam-pop resurgence after Bernard Butler’s exit.
Suede release Head Music.
Suede reunite for a charity show at the Royal Albert Hall.
Suede release their comeback album, Bloodsports.
Pulp release His ’n’ Hers.
Pulp release Different Class, featuring “Common People.”

Pulp release This Is Hardcore.
Jarvis Cocker invades the stage during Michael Jackson’s Brit Awards performance.
Pulp release We Love Life, produced by Scott Walker.
Pulp release More, their first album in more than two decades.
Elastica release their self-titled debut.
Elastica release their long-delayed second album, The Menace.
Supergrass release I Should Coco, including “Alright.”
Supergrass release In It for the Money.
The Verve release Urban Hymns, including “Bitter Sweet Symphony.”
Sleeper release their debut album, Smart.

Mansun release Attack of the Grey Lantern.
Ocean Colour Scene release Moseley Shoals.
Kula Shaker release K, a psychedelic Britpop-era success.
Manic Street Preachers release Everything Must Go.
“Three Lions” becomes England’s football anthem during the European Championship.
